column1: # MODE: PROD
# Which artifacts belong to which integration mode.
# A skill that offers more than one way to be driven declares it here, and
# `install.sh --integration <skill>=<mode>` picks one without a prompt, so an
# agent can choose its own interface headlessly.
# The rule is deliberately narrow: a binary named below installs ONLY in its
# mode, and every file not named installs in every mode. So SKILL.md, the
# schemas and the manpage are never mode-dependent, and a skill with no
# integration.tsv at all has one mode and is unaffected by the flag.
# `skill` is the default, because it is the interface that needs no client
# configuration and no running server -- which is what a `curl | bash` install
# has to leave working. `mcp` is opt-in: its tools are listed in every session
# that configures the server, so it is worth choosing rather than assuming.
# ai-text-editor-server is deliberately UNLISTED, not `skill`-only: both
# ai-text-editor (skill mode) and ai-text-editor-mcp (mcp mode) talk to it,
# and ai-text-editor-mcp's own autostart spawns it directly (looked up as a
# sibling of its own binary) whenever no server is already running --
# `open` in mcp mode is exactly the "no running server yet" case autostart
# exists for. Listing it as `skill`-only shipped an mcp-only install that
# could never open a fresh file: `cannot autostart ai-text-editor-server: No
# such file or directory`, confirmed by hand against a real mcp-mode install.
mode
skill
